newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SHOW JUMPING-ARGENTINE SAYS RIDERS INNOCENT.
newsitem.headline: SHOW JUMPING-ARGENTINE SAYS RIDERS INNOCENT.

text.p: The president of the Argentine Equestrian Federation said on Monday he believes in the innocence of four riders suspended for "severe cruelty" to their horses at this year's Olympics.
"I believe in what the riders told me at the time because there is no solid evidence," Jorge Gabriel told Reuters.
The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) announced in Switzerland that it was banning the four for making their horses jump over obstacles topped with wire and nails during training in Georgia.
"The FIE's proof or evidence is a blurred picture of an obstacle, where you can't make anything out," Gabriel said.
He added that the Argentine federation was not given sufficient opportunity to defend its riders.
The riders, Oscar Fuentes, Ricardo Kierkegard, Federico Castaing, and Justo Albarracin, have been banned for six months from November 1 and will be required to pay the costs of their hearing.
Argentina's federation will not act until the penalties have been confirmed, Gabriel said, adding: "I suppose the riders will appeal individually, and then we will see what happens."
The FIE said it was annulling the Olympic results of the Argentine team, which finished 17th.
Argentina is due to receive an International Olympic Committee delegation in late November as part of Buenos Aires' bid for the 2004 summer games.
